records.jp: 小さいころ、わたし、いじめられてたんだ。多分、ぼんやりしてるから。そして、他の子より発育が良かったから。わたし、泣いてることしかできなかった
records.en_original: I got bullied a lot when I was little. Maybe it was because I was a little spacey, or maybe it was because I hit my growth spurt before the other kids did. Either way, I spent most of my days crying.
records.en: I got bullied a lot when I was little. Maybe it was because I was a little spacey, or maybe it was because I hit my growth spurt before the other kids did. Either way, I spent most of my days crying.

records.jp: いじめられているわたしに、声をかけてくれる子がいたんだ。すっごく優しい子で……わたしたちは友達になって、一緒に遊ぶようになった
records.en_original: But there was one other kid who dared to approach a bullying victim like me... She was so kind. We quickly became friends and played together a lot.
records.en: But there was one other kid who dared to approach a bullying victim like me... She was so kind. We quickly became friends and played together a lot.

records.jp: あの子と秘密基地を作ることになったの。わたしたち二人だけの場所。基地を作っている間、毎日が楽しかった。けど、ある日男の子たちが、わたしたちの基地を壊そうと計画してる話を聞いちゃったんだ
records.en_original: That girl and I built a secret hideout together. A place for just the two of us. We had so much fun building it, and I wished that those days would never end. But one day, I overheard some boys talking about destroying our hideout.
records.en: That girl and I built a secret hideout together. A place for just the two of us. We had so much fun building it, and I wished that those days would never end. But one day, I overheard some boys talking about destroying our hideout.

records.jp: 男の子たちがわたしたちの基地を壊す。知ってたのに、わたしは怖くて何もできなかった。そんなわたしをあの子は怒ったんだ
records.en_original: I knew they were going to destroy our precious hideout, but I was paralyzed with fear. I couldn't do a thing to stop them. My friend got so mad at me...
records.en: I knew they were going to destroy our precious hideout, but I was paralyzed with fear. I couldn't do a thing to stop them. My friend got so mad at me...

records.jp: わたしはあの子みたいに強くないから、いじめっ子に対して逆らえない。そうやって嘆くわたしを見て、きっとがっかりしたんだ。突き放すようなことを^00言って、あの子は帰っちゃったの
records.en_original: I wasn't as strong as she was, so I couldn't stand up to the bullies. I'm sure she was really disappointed in me, seeing me downtrodden like that... So she just told me to forget about it and went home.
records.en: I wasn't strong like her, so I couldn't stand up to the bullies. She must have been disappointed to see me lamenting like that. She said something^00to push me away, then went home.

records.jp: 秘密基地が壊された日から、あの子は学校に来なくなった。そしてある日、学校からの帰り道で聞いちゃったんだ。あの子が、いじめっ子を殴って転校することになったって。きっと、わたしのために、あの子は……
records.en_original: She stopped coming to school after our secret hideout was destroyed. One day, when I was heading home from school, I finally heard why—she beat up one of the bullies and had to transfer schools. She did all of that for my sake...
records.en: She stopped coming to school after our secret hideout was destroyed. One day, when I was heading home from school, I finally heard why—she beat up one of the bullies and had to transfer schools. She did all of that for my sake...

records.jp: このまま離れ離れになるのはやだ。もう一度あの子に会いたくて、わたしは家に押しかけた。そこで、あの子の本当の気持ちを聞いたんだ。もっと頼ってほしかったって……
records.en_original: I couldn't stand the thought of leaving things like that, so I ran to her house to see her again. There, I found out how she really felt. She said she'd wanted me to rely on her more...
records.en: I couldn't stand the thought of leaving things like that, so I ran to her house to see her again. There, I found out how she really felt. She said she'd wanted me to rely on her more...

records.jp: わたしはあの子に嫌われたくなかったから、負担をかけまいとして頼れなかった。けど、それは間違ってたんだ。友達だから、頼って頼られて……それがあたりまえ。お互いの気持ちを話して、この時やっと、わたしたちは本当の友達になれたんだ
records.en_original: I didn't want her to hate me, so I never shared my problems with her before. I thought I was sparing her the trouble of dealing with them, but that isn't how friends are. Friends depend on one another. When we shared our feelings with one another that day, I believe we finally became true friends.
records.en: I didn't want her to hate me, so I never shared my problems with her before. I thought I was sparing her the trouble of dealing with them, but that isn't how friends are. Friends depend on one another. When we shared our feelings with one another that day, I believe we finally became true friends.

records.jp: 小さいころ、問題を起こしたわたしは転校することになりました。これ以上両親に迷惑はかけたくない、両親の役に立たなきゃ……そう思ったわたしは、以来ずっと家のお店の手伝いをしていました
records.en_original: When I was little, I caused some problems and had to transfer schools. I didn't want to cause my parents any more trouble and decided to help them in any way I could. That's why I started helping them around the cafe.
records.en: When I was little, I caused some problems and had to transfer schools. I didn't want to cause my parents any more trouble and decided to help them in any way I could. That's why I started helping them around the cafe.

records.jp: 遊びも習い事もせずにお店を手伝うわたしを見て、周りはよくできた娘だと^00言っていましたが、そこまでしなきゃ両親に申し訳が立たなかっただけなんです
records.en_original: I didn't study, I didn't play with friends, I dedicated all my time to helping out at the cafe. Everyone around me told I must be such a wonderful daughter, but really, it was the least I could do to make things up to my parents.
records.en: People called me a model daughter because I helped at the cafe instead of playing or taking lessons,^00but I only went that far because otherwise I couldn't face my parents.

records.jp: そんなある日、たまたま店に訪れた子とバレエの話を通じて友達になりました。何故だか話が弾んで……お店の手伝いも好きだということ、それでも同じ毎日を続けることに不安があること……いろんな話をしました
records.en_original: One day, I happened to strike up a conversation about ballet with this girl that visited our cafe. Somehow, I found myself talking to her about all kinds of things. Like how I enjoyed helping around the cafe, but worried that I would get stuck in that daily routine forever...
records.en: One day, I happened to strike up a conversation about ballet with this girl that visited our cafe. Somehow, I found myself talking to her about all kinds of things. Like how I enjoyed helping around the cafe, but worried that I would get stuck in that daily routine forever...

records.jp: お店に訪れたその子は、どうやらバレエのレッスンのために県外からわざわざやってきたみたいでした
records.en_original: It turned out that the cafe wasn't close to that girl's home—she traveled a long way to our area just for her ballet lessons.
records.en: It turned out that the cafe wasn't close to that girl's home—she traveled a long way to our area just for her ballet lessons.

records.jp: バレエが大好きなその子は、レッスンを受けるためにいろんな場所を飛び回っているそうです。お店に留まっていることしかできない自分には、そんな彼女がとても輝いて見えました
records.en_original: That girl loved ballet so dearly, she would travel all over the place to take lessons. To someone like me, who only ever saw the inside of the cafe, she was absolutely amazing.
records.en: That girl loved ballet so dearly, she would travel all over the place to take lessons. To someone like me, who only ever saw the inside of the cafe, she was absolutely amazing.

records.jp: その子とすっかり打ち解けた私は、ついお店の手伝いを続ける理由を話してしまいました
records.en_original: I felt like I could tell her anything, so it wasn't long before I revealed the reason I was always helping around the cafe.
records.en: I felt like I could tell her anything, so it wasn't long before I revealed the reason I was always helping around the cafe.

records.jp: わたしがお店を手伝う理由を話したからでしょうか。その子はわたしのことを遊びへと連れ出そうとするようになりました
records.en_original: It might have been because she heard why I was stuck at the cafe, but she started taking me to all sorts of places.
records.en: It might have been because she heard why I was stuck at the cafe, but she started taking me to all sorts of places.

records.jp: その子に連れられ、電車に乗り、ついには見たことのない都会まで出てきてしまいました。自分が進んでいるレールから外れることができなかったわたしを、その子は別の道へと連れて行ってくれたんです
records.en_original: She took me on the train and we rode it into the city, a place I had never seen. I had thought that I was stuck on the track I was on, but she showed me that there were other paths out there that I could take.
records.en: She took me on the train and we rode it into the city, a place I had never seen. I had thought that I was stuck on the track I was on, but she showed me that there were other paths out there that I could take.

records.jp: それから、その子と人生のレールの話をしました。みんな、それぞれのレールの上を進んでいる。みんな別のレールが気になるけど、脱線してしまったら戻れないかもしれない。わたしは思いました。もう少し自分のレールを進んでみようって。その先がどこに繋がっているのか、誰にもわからないんですから
records.en_original: After that, the two of us talked about our paths in life—how everybody is on their own set of tracks. Though we might be interested in switching tracks, we're afraid, as taking them might render us unable to return to what we know. I still didn't know what awaited me down the path I was on, but I decided to keep following it a little longer.
records.en: After that, the two of us talked about our paths in life—how everybody is on their own set of tracks. Though we might be interested in switching tracks, we're afraid, as taking them might render us unable to return to what we know. I still didn't know what awaited me down the path I was on, but I decided to keep following it a little longer.

records.jp: いつからバレエを始めたのか、実はあまり覚えていない。物心がついた時には、すでにバレエをしていたと思う。だから私にとって生きるというのはバレエをすることで、生きるのはとても楽しかった
records.en_original: I can't actually recall when I first started to do ballet. I've been doing it as long as I can remember. Ballet was my life, and life was good.
records.en: I can't actually recall when I first started to do ballet. I've been doing it as long as I can remember. Ballet was my life, and life was good.

records.jp: バレエを練習することで、生きるのがもっと楽しくなる。練習自体も楽しいから、私はずっと舞っていられた。それが普通じゃないんだって、今ならわかる
records.en_original: The more I practiced ballet, the more fun life was. I enjoyed practicing so much that I just danced non-stop. Though I know now that that wasn't a normal thing.
records.en: The more I practiced ballet, the more fun life was. I enjoyed practicing so much that I just danced non-stop. Though I know now that that wasn't a normal thing.

records.jp: そんな私も世界というものを知っていき、この才能が称賛されるだけのものではなく、嫉妬も生むのだとわかるくらいには大人になった。それでも、そんなことは関係なかった。私はバレエで生きていきたかった
records.en_original: As I grew older and came to understand the ways of the world, I realized that talent was not only met with praise, but also jealousy. Yet none of that mattered to me. I wanted to live for ballet, and ballet alone.
records.en: As I grew older and came to understand the ways of the world, I realized that talent was not only met with praise, but also jealousy. Yet none of that mattered to me. I wanted to live for ballet, and ballet alone.

records.jp: その日、私は一度死んだんだと思う。脚を故障して、一生バレエを踊ることができなくなったから。本来特待科へ進学するはずだった学校も、普通科になってしまった
records.en_original: I died that day. That terrible day when I broke my leg and was told that I could never dance again. The school I had so carefully selected for its special classes moved me to the regular class.
records.en: I think I died once that day. I injured my leg and would never be able to dance ballet again. Even at the school where I was supposed to enter the special scholarship course, I ended up in the regular course instead.

records.jp: 街で見かけた私と同じくらいの歳の子の話していることがわからなかった。バレエのない世界での生き方が私にはわからなかった。普通がわからなかった
records.en_original: I didn't know how to talk to other people my age. I didn't know how to live in a world without ballet. I didn't know how to be normal.
records.en: I couldn't understand what girls around my age were talking about when I saw them in town. I didn't know how to live in a world without ballet. I didn't understand what was normal.

records.jp: 勇気を出して外に出るけど、どこへ行っても「普通」が私を待ち受けている。それがとても恐ろしくて……息ができるのは、私の部屋の中だけ。普通って何だろう？　その答えを、この後私は知っていく
records.en_original: I tried to gather the courage to face the outside world, but no matter where I went, normality would be waiting for me. It was so terrifying, I could only breathe when I was alone in my room. What is "normal," anyway? I would soon find out.
records.en: I tried to gather the courage to face the outside world, but no matter where I went, normality would be waiting for me. It was so terrifying, I could only breathe when I was alone in my room. What is "normal," anyway? I would soon find out.

records.jp: 通い始めた学校で二人の女の子と出会った。それが、ユズとライム。二人との毎日が、灰色の私の日々を変えていった
records.en_original: I met these two girls at my new school, Yuzu and Lime. They brought light back into my dreary world.
records.en: I met these two girls at my new school, Yuzu and Lime. They brought light back into my dreary world.

records.jp: 二人との日々は、世の中の普通とはちょっと違ったのかもしれない。けど、一緒に過ごした時間が確実に私とこの世界を結んでいったんだ
records.en_original: The time we spent together may not have been normal to the average person, but it grounded me—it made me feel alive again.
records.en: The days I spent with them may have been a little different from what the world calls normal. But the time we shared steadily connected me to this world.

records.jp: 何でもない日々が、いつしかとても楽しいものになっていた。友達と呼べる子が、周りを囲んでいた。この世界で呼吸ができた。ユズとライムのおかげで私は今生きている。そのことを、絶対に忘れちゃいけないんだ
records.en_original: Those days we wasted together were some of the best I ever had. I was surrounded by people I could call my friends. I finally felt like I could breathe again. Yuzu and Lime are the reason I'm alive today, and I will never forget that.
records.en: Before I knew it, those ordinary days had become something I truly enjoyed. I was surrounded by girls I could call friends. I could breathe in this world. Yuzu and Lime are the reason I am alive now. I must never forget that.

records.jp: 私の父は灯台守。だから、私も海の見える街に住んでた。そんなある日、一人で海を見ていたところに声をかけてきたのが、金城勇希という女の子。最近^00引っ越してきたというその子は、会うたびに他愛のない話をしてきた。一方的にぐいぐい話しかけてくるの、最初はすごく戸惑ってたんだから
records.en_original: My father is a lighthouse keeper. That's why we lived in a town so close to the ocean. One day, a girl named Yuki Kinjo called out to me while I was staring at the sea. This girl, who said she had just moved there, would always talk about such silly things whenever we met. She'd carry the whole conversation on her own. I didn't know what to make of her at first.
records.en: My father is a lighthouse keeper, so I lived in a town overlooking the sea. One day, while I was watching the ocean alone, a girl named Kinjou Yuki spoke to me. She had recently^00moved there and would chat with me about trivial things whenever we met. At first, I was bewildered by how boldly she kept striking up conversations with me.

records.jp: 容姿がそれなりに整っているのは自覚していた。だから、男の子から告白されても特に何も感じなかった。何も感じないから、付き合うのは断った。もっとオブラートに包めと勇希には言われたけどね。嘘をつくのは、今でも苦手だ
records.en_original: I knew I wasn't bad-looking. So, when a boy told me he had feelings for me, I didn't feel any particular way about it. I simply didn't feel the same way, so I turned him down. Yuki said I could've sugarcoated my rejection a bit, but I'm no good at lying, even now.
records.en: I knew I wasn't bad-looking. So, when a boy told me he had feelings for me, I didn't feel any particular way about it. I simply didn't feel the same way, so I turned him down. Yuki said I could've sugarcoated my rejection a bit, but I'm no good at lying, even now.

records.jp: 勇希に教えてもらった、モヤモヤを解決する方法、今でも覚えてる。それは大声を出すこと。私は臆病で恥ずかしがり屋だから、勇希がそばにいるときじゃないとこんなことできないんだ
records.en_original: I still remember the stress relief method that Yuki taught me. All you have to do is scream and let it all out. I'm much too shy to do that on my own, though, so I can only do it if she's there with me.
records.en: I still remember the stress relief method that Yuki taught me. All you have to do is scream and let it all out. I'm much too shy to do that on my own, though, so I can only do it if she's there with me.

records.jp: 連絡先を交換して、頻繁に会うようになって……いろいろ自分のことを話す仲になった。その時には、もう私は私の気持ちを自覚してたんだと思う。ねえ、知ってた？　勇希が遠くを見てるとき、あくびして目を閉じてるとき、眠くてうとうとしてるとき。私はずっと、勇希の顔を眺めてた
records.en_original: We exchanged information and started seeing each other more often... We started talking about all kinds of personal stuff. I think I already knew how I felt about her at that point. I was always stealing glances. When she stared off into the distance, when she'd yawn and shut her eyes, when she got tired and started nodding off. Always.
records.en: We exchanged contact information, began meeting frequently, and grew close enough to tell each other all sorts of personal things. By then, I think I already understood my feelings. Did you know, Yuki? Whenever you gazed into the distance, closed your eyes to yawn, or nodded off sleepily, I was always watching your face.

records.jp: 勇希のことをずっと見てたから、私は気が付いたんだ。勇希が何かを隠していることを。私はそれが知りたかった
records.en_original: I'd watched her long enough to know that something was wrong. I knew she was hiding something, and I wanted to know what it was.
records.en: I'd watched her long enough to know that something was wrong. I knew she was hiding something, and I wanted to know what it was.

records.jp: 勇希と星を見る約束をした。私の大好きなものを、大好きな人と見る。最高の夜になるはずだった
records.en_original: We made a promise to look at the stars together. I was going to see my favorite thing with my favorite person in the entire world. It was going to be the perfect night.
records.en: We made a promise to look at the stars together. I was going to see my favorite thing with my favorite person in the entire world. It was going to be the perfect night.

records.jp: 電話もフリスぺも通じない。街のどこを探しても勇希は見当たらない。こんなことになるなら、好きだなんて伝えなければよかった。きっと勇希と私の気持ちは違っていて、だから勇希は私から逃げたんだって、何度も何度も自分を責めた
records.en_original: She didn't respond to any of my calls or FreeSpace messages. I couldn't find her anywhere in town. If I had known this would happen, I never would have confessed my feelings for her. I figured she ran away from me because she didn't feel the same way. I kicked myself again and again for chasing her away.
records.en: She didn't respond to any of my calls or FreeSpace messages. I couldn't find her anywhere in town. If I had known this would happen, I never would have confessed my feelings for her. I figured she ran away from me because she didn't feel the same way. I kicked myself again and again for chasing her away.

records.jp: そしてとうとう、勇希のことを知る人を見つけた。その人の話を聞いたことで、私は勇希の隠していたことと、本当の気持ちを知ることになる
records.en_original: I finally found someone who knew Yuki too. I listened to what they had to say, and came to understand her true feelings and the things she had been hiding.
records.en: I finally found someone who knew Yuki too. I listened to what they had to say, and came to understand her true feelings and the things she had been hiding.

records.jp: 小さいころ、普通の人に聞こえない声が聞こえるきららは、周りの子供たちからいじめられていた。普通と違う人は何かと迫害を受けるもの。だからしょーがない。そう思っていた
records.en_original: Ever since I was little, I could hear a voice that no one else could hear. The other children would bully me because of that. I figured there was nothing I could do about it. Those who are different get persecuted by those who are not. That's all there is to it.
records.en: Since childhood, Kirara could hear a voice ordinary people could not, and the other children bullied her for it. People who differ from the norm are often persecuted. Kirara thought there was nothing to be done about it.

records.jp: きららの聞こえる声のことは、パパも信じてくれなかった。家でもきららは一人だった
records.en_original: Not even my own father believed me when I told him about the voice. I was all alone, even amongst my own family.
records.en: Papa didn't believe Kirara about the voice she could hear either. Kirara was alone even at home.

records.jp: そんなとき、ユカという女の子と出会った。ユカもまた、一人だった。似た者同士が出会って、きららとユカは友達になった
records.en_original: That's when I met Yuka. She was alone, just like me. I had finally found a kindred spirit, and soon we became friends.
records.en: That was when Kirara met a girl named Yuka. Yuka was alone too. Two similar girls found each other, and Kirara and Yuka became friends.

records.jp: ユカはきららに聞こえている声のことを信じてくれた。二人で声について話しているうちに、この声が未来の予言をしているかもしれないことが分かった。誰がきららたちの話を聞いていたのかはわからないが、予言の話はいつの間にか村中に広がっていた
records.en_original: Yuka believed me when I told her about the voice. After discussing it, we thought it may actually be predicting the future. I'm not sure who overheard, but word of the prophetic girl soon spread all throughout town.
records.en: Yuka believed Kirara when she told her about the voice. As they talked about it, they realized the voice might be predicting the future. Kirara does not know who overheard them, but before long, word of the prophecies had spread throughout the village.

records.jp: きららが聞いている声のことを、いつしかみんな神の声と言うようになった。パパもきららに対する態度を一変させ、きららの生活は大きく変わった
records.en_original: Suddenly, everyone started saying it was the voice of the Divine. Even my father changed his attitude towards me. My life changed dramatically after that.
records.en: Suddenly, everyone started saying it was the voice of the Divine. Even my father changed his attitude towards me. My life changed dramatically after that.

records.jp: きららの予言を使ってパパは商売を始めた。日に日にきららたちの生活は豊かになっていった。パパもきららを見てくれるし、褒めてくれる。よかったと思う反面、どこかすっきりしない自分もいた
records.en_original: My father used my prophecies to start a business. Our lives became more comfortable day by day. He was finally paying attention to me, even praising me. I was glad, but an anxiety started to stir in my gut.
records.en: Papa used Kirara's prophecies to start a business. Kirara and her family's lives grew richer by the day. Papa finally looked at Kirara and praised her. Part of Kirara was glad, but another part still felt uneasy.

records.jp: そうしていつの間にか、久野家は村の中で大きな力を持つ存在になっていた。今まできららを無視していた人たちが、じろじろときららを見るようになった。その視線は、正直気持ちの良いものではなかったな
records.en_original: Before I knew it, our family became very influential in our town. People who had previously ignored me now watched me as I walked down the street. Their stares made me feel ill at ease.
records.en: Before long, the Kuno family had gained great influence in the village. People who once ignored Kirara began staring at her. To be honest, Kirara did not like the way they looked at her.

records.jp: 気が付くとユカと会える時間が減っていた。喜んでくれる人がいるから予言をしていたが、本当はそんなのどーでもよくて、きららはずっとユカと遊んでいたかった
records.en_original: I couldn't see Yuka as often anymore. I was busy making prophecies because it made people happy, but all I truly wanted to do was play with Yuka.
records.en: Before long, Kirara had less and less time to see Yuka. She made prophecies because they made people happy, but none of that truly mattered to her. Kirara only wanted to keep playing with Yuka.

records.jp: 村にはケイタという少年がいた。ケイタは村長の息子で、親が偉いからってわがままし放題。ケイタと村長には、きららのパパも強く出られないようだった
records.en_original: Keita was the mayor's son. He thought he was special just because his parents were important. To them, my father and I were nothing.
records.en: There was a boy in Kirara's village named Keita. He was the village head's son and did whatever he pleased because his father was important. Even Kirara's Papa seemed unable to stand up to Keita or the village head.

records.jp: きららの村は老人が多く、老人たちは村の宝であるツボをとにかく大事にしていた
records.en_original: There were a lot of elderly folks in our village, and they felt very strongly about this sacred urn, one of our village's heirlooms.
records.en: Kirara's village had many elderly residents, and they treasured an urn regarded as the village's treasure above all else.

records.jp: パパはこの村で得た名声ときららの力を利用して、県知事になろうと企んでいた。だから、村の老人たちを味方につけなくちゃいけない。そんな中、ある事件が起きて……きららは本当に大事なものを守るため、勇気を振り絞ったんだ
records.en_original: My father wanted to capitalize on my fame to become governor. Having the elderly on his side was vital to his success. That's when the incident happened...and I had to muster up the courage to protect what was truly important.
records.en: Papa planned to use the fame he gained in the village and Kirara's power to become governor. To do that, he needed the village elders on his side. Then an incident occurred... and Kirara gathered her courage to protect what truly mattered.

records.jp: お父さんのことはよく覚えていない。物心がつく前に死んじゃったから。だから私にとっての家族は、お母さんとお姉ちゃんだけだった。記憶に残っているお母さんはいつも誰かに頭を下げていて……私たち姉妹を女手一つで育てるのは大変だったと思う
records.en_original: I don't really remember my father. He died when I was very young, so it was always just Mom, my older sister, and me. Mom was always putting herself down, so in my memories, she's always bowing her head... I think it must've been hard for her to raise both of us as a single mom.
records.en: I don't remember Dad very well. He died before I was old enough to remember, so to me, family meant only Mom and Onee-chan. In my memories, Mom was always bowing her head to someone... It must have been hard for her to raise the two of us alone.

records.jp: お母さんを喜ばせたくて、誕生日にケーキを作ってみたんだ。見た目は不格好だったけど、美味しくできたと思う。でも、お母さん、全然嬉しそうじゃな^00かったな。この時もっと違う言葉をかけてれば……今ならそう思う
records.en_original: I wanted to make Mom happy, so one year I made her a birthday cake. It didn't look the prettiest, but I thought it was still plenty delicious! But Mom didn't look happy at all when I gave it to her. Even now, I wonder what would've happened if I had said something different back then... Would it have changed anything?
records.en: I wanted to make Mom happy, so I made her a birthday cake. It looked clumsy, but I thought it tasted good. Mom did not look happy^00at all, though. Now I think that perhaps I should have said something different then.

records.jp: きっといろんなものにお母さん追い詰められていたんだ。「電球を買ってきます」そう言って、二度と家には戻ってこなかった。周りから見たらダメな母親だったのかもしれない。それでも、私たちはお母さんが大好きだった
records.en_original: I'm sure Mom was under all kinds of pressure. One day she told us that she was going out to buy a light bulb...and never came back. I'm sure she looked like a terrible mother to everyone else. But we still loved her.
records.en: Mom must have been cornered by all kinds of things. She said, 'I'm going to buy a light bulb,' and never came home. To everyone else, she may have looked like a terrible mother. Even so, we loved Mom.

records.jp: いくら探しても、お母さんは見つからなかった。私たちはお母さんにとってお荷物で、捨てられてしまったのかもしれない。そんな考えが頭をよぎったけれど、世界がそんな悲しいものだなんて陽桜莉には絶対思ってほしくなかった
records.en_original: We couldn't find her, no matter how hard we looked. Maybe we were just baggage that weighed her down, and she finally decided to throw us away one day. That was all I could think...but I didn't want Hiori to believe the world was such a cruel place.
records.en: No matter how hard we searched, we couldn't find Mom. Maybe we were a burden to her and she'd abandoned us. The thought crossed my mind, but I never wanted Hiori to believe the world was such a sad place.

records.jp: そうして年月は過ぎ、私たちが現実を受け入れる強さを持ったころ。幼き日の傷と向き合うため、私たちは改めてお母さんを探し始めた。そんなとき、立ちふさがったのが詩だった
records.en_original: Years passed before we gathered the strength to accept reality. In order to face the scars that marred our childhood, we began to search for our mother once more. This time, Uta was the one who stood in our way.
records.en: Years passed, and once we were strong enough to accept reality, we began searching for Mom again to face the wounds of our childhood. That was when Uta stood in our way.

records.jp: 詩はどういう手を使ってか、私たちの過去を調べ上げ、的確に傷を抉ってきた。私たちが苦しむ姿を見たかったそう。詩は私たちがお母さんと再会することで、より大きな絶望を味わうことになると思っていたようだけど、残念ね。この世界は、あなたが思うより優しさであふれてる
records.en_original: Somehow, Uta had dug up our past and knew exactly how to gouge open our old wounds. She wanted to see us suffer. I think she believed that meeting our mother would cause us to fall into even greater despair. Unfortunately for her, this world is much kinder than she thought.
records.en: Somehow, Uta dug up our past and struck precisely at our wounds. She wanted to see us suffer. She seemed to think reuniting with Mom would plunge us into even greater despair, but unfortunately for her, this world is kinder than she thinks.

records.jp: 私の祖母の記憶……でしょうか？　断片的すぎて、何も思い出せません……
records.en_original: A memory about my grandmother...I think? It is too fragmented for me to remember...
records.en: A memory of my grandmother...perhaps? It is too fragmented for me to remember anything...

records.jp: 祖母から不思議な子、と言われていたようです
records.en_original: It seems my grandmother used to tell me that I was "interesting."
records.en: It seems she used to call me a strange child.

records.jp: 祖母は私に好かれたかったみたいです
records.en_original: I think she wanted me to like her.
records.en: I think she wanted me to like her.

records.jp: ひまわり……その言葉を聞くと、なぜだか不思議な気持ちになります
records.en_original: Sunflowers... Whenever someone mentions sunflowers, this strange feeling wells up inside of me.
records.en: Sunflowers... Whenever someone mentions sunflowers, this strange feeling wells up inside of me.

records.jp: これは、昔の私……でしょうか？　自分のことなのに、何もわかりません……
records.en_original: Is this...who I used to be? These may be my memories, but I don't understand a thing...
records.en: Is this...who I used to be? These may be my memories, but I don't understand a thing...

records.jp: ごめんなさい、何がわからないのか、わからないんです
records.en_original: I'm sorry. I don't even know what it is I don't understand.
records.en: I'm sorry. I don't even know what it is I don't understand.

records.jp: 小さいころから病弱で、いつも病院のお世話になってた。体調が良くなって退院しても、少ししたらまた病院へ戻る。その繰り返し。きっと死ぬまでずっと、その繰り返し。毎回落ち込んでたら、見てる方もうんざりしちゃうでしょ？　だからあたしは、毎日笑顔の練習をする
records.en_original: I've always had a weak immune system, so I spent a lot of my childhood in the hospital. Even if I got well enough to be discharged, I'd end up going back before long. A never-ending cycle that I was set to repeat till the day I died. I realized that the people around me would get tired of me if I was just depressed all the time, so I practiced smiling every day.
records.en: I had been frail since childhood and was always in and out of hospitals. Even after getting well enough to be discharged, I would return before long. The same cycle again and again—probably until the day I died. Everyone around me would get sick of it if I got depressed every time, right? So I practiced smiling every day.

records.jp: この後の人生にある程度覚悟があるとはいえ、普通の生活に憧れちゃうのは仕方がないよね。もしあたしが学校に通ってたら、どんな友達ができてたかな？あたしはみんなにどう思われてたかな？　そんなことを考えて、日々をやり過ごしてた
records.en_original: I knew what life had in store for me, but I couldn't help but long for a normal life. If I could go to school, who would my friends be? What would everyone think of me? I spent my days fantasizing about things like that.
records.en: I knew what life had in store for me, but I couldn't help but long for a normal life. If I could go to school, who would my friends be? What would everyone think of me? I spent my days fantasizing about things like that.

records.jp: あたしの主治医には、本当の気持ちがばれてたみたい。やっぱりお医者さんって頭がいいや
records.en_original: Looks like my doctor figured out how I was really feeling. I guess doctors really are smart.
records.en: Looks like my doctor figured out how I was really feeling. I guess doctors really are smart.

records.jp: 今までにない症状が出たあたしは、その治療のため新しい病院へと引越しをする。そこで、あたしは伶那と出会った
records.en_original: I developed new symptoms that I hadn't had before, and I had to move to a new hospital for the cure. That's where I met Rena.
records.en: New symptoms appeared, so I moved to a different hospital to receive treatment. That was where I met Rena.

records.jp: 伶那に対しては複雑な想いを抱いていたけど、一緒に過ごすうちにその想いは少しずつ変わっていった。伶那が嘘で塗り固められたあたしの本当の姿を、見ようとしてくれているってわかったから
records.en_original: I wasn't sure how I felt about Rena at first, but my feelings for her changed as we spent more time together. I realized that she was trying to see the real me, the one I had buried under a mountain of lies.
records.en: I wasn't sure how I felt about Rena at first, but my feelings for her changed as we spent more time together. I realized that she was trying to see the real me, the one I had buried under a mountain of lies.

records.jp: 灰って突然空間に現れるから、窓を閉め切っても意味がないんだってね。ふざけんな。^00^00けど、この話を聞いたらきっと伶那の方がふざけんなって泣きわめくんだろうな。きっとあたしなんかのために人生を無駄にしちゃうんだろうな。そう思ったから手紙まで残したのに、伶那ってばほんと、しつこいんだから
records.en_original: Apparently this Ash stuff could randomly appear in the air, so closing the windows wouldn't make a difference. So that sucked. But I knew it would suck even more when Rena found out—she'd freak out, maybe even cry... I didn't want her to waste her life on someone like me, so I left her a letter. Only I didn't realize just how persistent she could be.
records.en: Ash just appears out of nowhere, so apparently even sealing every window would not help. You've got to be kidding me.^00^00But if Rena heard that, she'd probably be the one crying and screaming, ‘You've got to be kidding me!’ She'd waste her whole life on someone like me. That's why I even left her a letter, but Rena really is so stubborn.

records.jp: 平凡な私は、平凡な毎日を送る。休日も、友達の誘いがなければ、家でゴロゴロ。こうやって客観的にみると、もったいない日々を送ってたよなあ。でも、普通から抜け出すために何かしようだなんて、私は思いもしなかったんだ
records.en_original: I was just an ordinary girl, living an ordinary life. If none of my friends asked me to hang out, I'd just laze around at home. Looking back on it objectively, I guess I was kinda wasting my life, but I never once thought about doing something to break out of my totally normal existence.
records.en: I was just an ordinary girl, living an ordinary life. If none of my friends asked me to hang out, I'd just laze around at home. Looking back on it objectively, I guess I was kinda wasting my life, but I never once thought about doing something to break out of my totally normal existence.

records.jp: テレビにはいろんな世界が映されている。それを見て、泣いたり笑ったりする。その世界は、私たちがいる世界と同じなはずなのに、どうしてだろうね。どこか別世界の話で、私はテレビに出るような人と同じにはなれないってずっと^00思ってた
records.en_original: I saw all kinds of different worlds on TV. They would make me laugh, make me cry... On some level, I knew that each world I saw on TV was the same as the one I lived in, but for some reason I couldn't imagine being like the people I saw onscreen. It was like they were in a whole different universe.
records.en: Television showed me all kinds of worlds. I laughed and cried while watching them. Those worlds should have been part of the same world I lived in, so why did they feel like somewhere else entirely? I always^00thought I could never become someone like the people on TV.

records.jp: スマホを落としたことに気が付いて、来た道を戻ったんだよね。幸い盗まれることなくコンビニの前に落ちてたけど……私、ちゃんとポケットにしまった気が……
records.en_original: I noticed I lost my phone and ran back to find it. Luckily, no one had taken it, and it was on the ground in front of the convenience store... But I could've sworn that I'd put it in my pocket...
records.en: I noticed I lost my phone and ran back to find it. Luckily, no one had taken it, and it was on the ground in front of the convenience store... But I could've sworn that I'd put it in my pocket...

records.jp: 私の記憶にない場所で、何かしている私たち……そんな光景が頭の中に飛び込んできた。どうしてココロトープでこんな光景が？　みんな忘れているだけで、私たちはこの場所に行ったことがある……？
records.en_original: That was us, doing something in a place I don't remember... Why did I suddenly see that? What's it doing in my Heartscape? Have we been to this place before and forgotten about it...?
records.en: That was us, doing something in a place I don't remember... Why did I suddenly see that? What's it doing in my Heartscape? Have we been to this place before and forgotten about it...?

records.jp: 私の知らない場所の記憶だ。ココロトープは、記憶や想いが形になった世界^00……。これも、私の記憶……ってこと？
records.en_original: A memory of a place I don't remember. The Heartscape is where memories and emotions take shape... So does that mean this is one of my memories too...?
records.en: A memory of a place I do not know. A Heartscape is a world where memories and feelings take form^00... Does that mean this is my memory too?

records.jp: 私はどうやら、共感能力に欠ける人間のようです。昔からそうで、祖母が孫である私に会えるのが嬉しいという感覚がまったく分かりませんでした
records.en_original: It seems that I was born without empathy. My grandmother was always happy to see me, but I couldn't understand such feelings at all.
records.en: It seems I am a person who lacks empathy. I had been that way for as long as I can remember; I could not understand why my grandmother was happy simply to see her granddaughter.

records.jp: 私は祖母と会うことで特別な感情を抱くことはありませんでした。両親と会う時も、学校で同級生と会う時も、それは変わりません。ただ、私と違う存在と会うだけ。気持ちが揺れることなど、あるでしょうか？
records.en_original: Seeing my grandmother didn't arouse happiness or any other emotion within me. The same went for my parents and my classmates too. I was simply coming into contact with an entity that existed outside of myself, was that supposed to evoke some kind of emotion in me?
records.en: Meeting my grandmother did not stir any special emotion in me. The same was true when I met my parents or classmates. I was simply encountering beings different from myself. Why should that make my feelings waver?

records.jp: 人に好かれたいと思う気持ちが、私にはわかりませんでした。今も……そうかもしれません
records.en_original: I could never understand the desire to be liked by others. Even now, I still don't understand...
records.en: I could never understand the desire to be liked by others. Even now, I still don't understand...

records.jp: その時ひまわりをじっと見たのは、まぶしい黄色が目についたので、その色の出所を見つめていただけでした。それを見て、祖母は私がひまわりが好きなのだと誤解したのです
records.en_original: One time, my grandmother caught me staring at a bunch of sunflowers. A bright yellow flash of color had caught my eye, so I was just looking for its source. But my grandmother misunderstood and assumed I was staring at them because I loved sunflowers.
records.en: One time, my grandmother caught me staring at a bunch of sunflowers. A bright yellow flash of color had caught my eye, so I was just looking for its source. But my grandmother misunderstood and assumed I was staring at them because I loved sunflowers.

records.jp: 祖母のことは、好きでも嫌いでもありませんでした。ただ、誤解されているのが面倒だと感じていました。面倒なら、わざわざ会う理由はありません
records.en_original: I didn't like or dislike my grandmother. But I did find this misunderstanding very annoying. Since dealing with it was a hassle, I figured there was no reason to keep seeing her.
records.en: I didn't like or dislike my grandmother. But I did find this misunderstanding very annoying. Since dealing with it was a hassle, I figured there was no reason to keep seeing her.

records.jp: 祖母が私と会いたがっていると母から言われますが、私には祖母の気持ちなど分かりませんでした。人の気持ちなど分からないものでしょう？
records.en_original: My mother told me that my grandmother wanted to see me, but I couldn't understand why. How was I supposed to understand another person's feelings?
records.en: My mother told me that my grandmother wanted to see me, but I couldn't understand why. How was I supposed to understand another person's feelings?

records.jp: わからないものを当たり前のようにわかれと言ってくる世の中が、苦しかったのを覚えています。私にはわかりませんでした。私がおかしいのか、世界がおかしいのか
records.en_original: I remember how harsh it was to live in a world where everybody takes for granted the things you don't understand. I didn't understand anything. Am I crazy? Or is it the world that's crazy?
records.en: I remember how painful it was to live in a world that expected me to understand things I could not as though they were obvious. I did not understand. Was something wrong with me, or with the world?

records.jp: 同級生からも、私は変わっているとよく言われていました。そういう風に扱われるのが面倒だったので、私は人との衝突をやり過ごす術を磨くことにしたんです。微笑みを絶やさないこと。疑問は抱かず、常に人に同調すること。そうしていれば、少なくとも私は空気になれました
records.en_original: My classmates often told me I was weird. It was annoying to be treated that way, so I tried to improve my interpersonal skills. Always keep smiling. Nod along without questioning anything. Doing that at least helped me fit in a little better.
records.en: My classmates often told me I was strange. Being treated that way was troublesome, so I refined ways to avoid conflict with others: never stop smiling, never question anything, and always agree. As long as I did that, I could at least fade into the background.

records.jp: 会わないうちに祖母は亡くなっていました。祖母の家の周りに残されていたのは、数えきれないほどの黄色。その黄色がまぶしくて、目に焼き付いて……今でも私の心をざわつかせるのです
records.en_original: My grandmother passed away before I saw her again. Her house was enveloped by a sea of yellow. That dazzling yellow image seared itself into my mind... Even now, remembering it makes my heart ache.
records.en: My grandmother died before I saw her again. Countless patches of yellow remained around her house. That dazzling yellow burned itself into my eyes... Even now, it unsettles my heart.

records.jp: この世界にやってきてからの記憶。水に囲まれた学校での生活は、平凡な私がずっと望んでいた非日常だった
records.en_original: Memories of my time in this world. I always wanted something to set myself apart. My life here was just what I was looking for.
records.en: Memories from after I arrived in this world. Life at a school surrounded by water was the extraordinary experience that someone as ordinary as me had always longed for.

records.jp: 望んでいたからと言って、その非日常が良いものとは限らない。見知らぬ世界に迷い込んだ寂しさ、そして直面する危機……。辛くて泣くこともあった。けど、それでも、みんなと過ごす日々は楽しかった
records.en_original: Though it wasn't all fun and games. It was scary finding myself in a strange world, not to mention the danger that was there... Sometimes I felt so lonely, I cried. Even so, the days I spent with everyone were so much fun.
records.en: Wanting something extraordinary did not mean it would necessarily be good. There was the loneliness of being lost in an unfamiliar world and the dangers we faced... Sometimes it hurt so much that I cried. Even so, the days I spent with everyone were fun.

records.jp: 恥ずかしくてごまかしたけど……これだけは間違いないよ。みんなと会えて私は幸せだ
records.en_original: I may have hid it because I felt embarrassed, but... I'm so glad I met everyone here.
records.en: I was embarrassed and tried to play it off...but one thing is certain. Meeting everyone made me happy.
